worksheet.title: What Comes First?
worksheet.subtitle: Finding the step that starts it all
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the step that must happen first.

parts.title: Some steps must come first
parts.text: You cannot slide down before you climb up! Some steps have to happen FIRST. Help Bit find the step that comes first.

parts.title: Watch Bit go down the slide
parts.note: First climb up ⬆, then slide down ⬇. Up comes first.

parts.title: Climb the ladder
parts.prompt: To get to the top, what comes first? Circle it.   ⬆ climb up    ⬇ come down

parts.title: Go through the door
parts.prompt: Bit wants to go through the door. What comes first? Circle it.   (a) open the door    (b) walk through  ➡

parts.title: You try — get ready
parts.prompt: Which comes first when you get dressed? Circle it.   1) put on a sock    2) put on a shoe

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Finding the first step is how you start a plan. If you do steps out of order, the plan does not work.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children identify the step that must happen first in a two-step action. Recognizing the starting step — and that some steps depend on earlier ones — is essential to building a correct sequence or algorithm.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children reason about the order in which steps must occur.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles the first step.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: act out each two-step action so children feel the order.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: the slide — 'you must climb up BEFORE you slide down.' First is ⬆.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — to get to the top, climb up comes first.
3. YOU TRY: children pick the first step for the door (open) and for getting dressed (sock).
4. Connect: 'If you do steps out of order, the plan does not work — order matters.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Model — slide: first ⬆ climb up, then ⬇ slide down.
Ex 1 — circle ⬆ climb up.   Ex 2 — circle 'open the door'.
Ex 3 — circle 'put on a sock' (the sock goes on before the shoe).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: picking the more exciting step (the slide!) — ask 'but what has to happen first?'
Simplify: physically act out the two steps in order, then ask which was first.
Extend: ask what comes LAST, or add a middle step (climb, sit, slide).
Movement option: do 'shoes' as a class — everyone mimes sock first, then shoe.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child circles the step that must happen first in each pair and can explain why it cannot be skipped.
